rows.narration: You can spend a fortune on a room and still have it feel unfinished, and you can spend very little and have it feel considered.
In this video we are going through 3 of them, one at a time, with the reasoning behind each one and exactly how to apply it in a real home.
Number 1. Keep the palette continuous between rooms. There is a real principle underneath this. Homes feel bigger and calmer when one room flows into the next.
A different scheme behind every door makes a house feel like a corridor of unrelated boxes. The way to actually do this is simple.
Use one base color throughout and change only the accents room to room. Sightlines between spaces are where this matters most.
Do this one thing and the rest of the room starts to make more sense.
That brings us to number 2. Match the coffee table height to the sofa seat. The thinking behind this is simple.
A table much lower than the seat forces an uncomfortable reach, and one much higher blocks the view across the room. Here is how to apply it.
Aim within an inch or two of the sofa seat height, and choose a length roughly two-thirds of the sofa. Round tables work better in tight or high-traffic rooms.
Idea number 3. Hang your curtains close to the ceiling, not to the window frame. This works for a specific reason.

rows.narration: The eye reads the top of the curtain rod as the top of the wall, so mounting the rod high stretches the whole room upward and makes a standard eight-foot ceiling feel far taller than it is.
Here is how to apply it. Mount the rod four to six inches below the ceiling line and let the panels break just barely on the floor.
Buy the longest ready-made length you can find, usually ninety-six or one hundred and eight inches, and widen the rod so the panels stack off the glass.
That is all 3 of them. If you found something here worth trying, there are more videos like this on the channel.
